pinterest.title: Who Can Perform a Marriage in Australia? The 4 Types of Authorised Celebrant
pinterest.description: Who can perform a marriage in Australia is fixed by law. As at November 2026, only an authorised marriage celebrant can legally marry you, and there are four types: Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants, Commonwealth-registered religious marriage celebrants, ministers of religion from a recognised denomination, and state and territory officers. Our guide explains each type and how to check yours on the official register.

pinterest.title: What Your Marriage Celebrant Must Do to Make It Legal
pinterest.description: From the Notice of Intended Marriage to the certificates: your authorised celebrant must meet each of you separately and in person, be physically present with you and 2 witnesses over 18, and submit the paperwork to the registry within 14 days. As at November 2026, the NOIM must reach your celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding. Read the full guide.

pinterest.title: Who Can Marry You If Your Wedding Is Overseas?
pinterest.description: Planning a destination wedding? As at November 2026, an Australian-authorised marriage celebrant cannot perform a marriage overseas. You can marry legally at home with your celebrant and celebrate abroad, or marry under the destination's own rules, which often include a certificate of no impediment. Our guide explains both paths and who can legally marry you.

instagram_carousel.caption:
Who can legally marry you in Australia? The answer is a short list, and it is fixed by law.

As at November 2026, you must be married by an authorised marriage celebrant to be legally married here. There are four types: Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants, Commonwealth-registered religious marriage celebrants, ministers of religion from a recognised denomination, and state and territory officers.

Hoping a friend or sibling will marry you? They can, but only once registered as a celebrant. Registration is not automatic, and AGD has up to 6 months to assess a completed application. The simpler route is to book an authorised celebrant and ask how your friend can take part in the ceremony.

Before you pay a deposit, check your celebrant on AGD's Register of Marriage Celebrants. Each entry shows their registration status and whether they perform civil ceremonies or are a religious marriage celebrant.

Celebrating overseas? An Australian-authorised celebrant cannot perform a marriage abroad. You can marry legally at home first and celebrate overseas, or marry under the destination's own rules.

Our new guide covers each celebrant type, the legal steps your celebrant must follow and who can marry you abroad.

The legal ceremony stays with you and your celebrant. The celebration is where we come in. Send us a message and your Wedded Advisor, one person from start to finish, will plan the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, in your time zone. Full guide at the link in our bio.
